  "text": "The laundrette on Mercer Street had one machine that washed things out of memory.

A handwritten notice above it said: CHECK ALL POCKETS.

Mara brought the yellow cardigan she had worn when her sister stopped speaking to her. She fed in six coins and watched the sleeves turn behind the glass.

Afterward, she remembered the argument but not the sentence that had ended it.

This seemed like mercy.

The next week she washed a tablecloth. Then a scarf. By November, she could think of her sister without feeling the old heat rise through her neck.

She could not remember why they had quarreled.

At Christmas, a parcel arrived containing a blue bowl, carefully mended. Mara recognized it as their mother's, though she had thought it was green.

Under the bowl lay a note.

I shouldn't have thrown it. I'm sorry.

Mara took the note to the laundrette.

The attendant was emptying lint into a bin.

“Does it work on paper?” Mara asked.

“It works on anything.”

“And can you get things back?”

He looked at the note in her hand.

“Not here.”

She stood beside the machine until someone asked whether she was using it. Then she put her coins away.

At home, she called her sister.

“I got the bowl,” she said.

“I wasn't sure you'd want it.”

Mara traced a repaired crack with her thumb.

“I've forgotten some things,” she said. “What I said to you.”

Her sister was quiet.

“Do you want me to tell you?”

Mara pulled out a chair. Through the window, she could see the laundrette sign switching off.

“Yes,” she said, and sat down."
